business.title: Research on the mechanical properties and freeze resistance of geopolymer concrete
business.description: To investigate the mechanical properties and freeze resistance of fiber-reinforced geopolymer concrete, this paper uses kaolin, slag powder, and fly ash as the silicate-aluminate cementitious materials, sodium silicate and sodium hydroxide as the alkaline activators, The alkali activator dosage was adjusted to optimize the performance of different silica-alumina cementitious materials. Polypropylene fibers with lengths of 9 mm and 18 mm were blended as reinforcement to prepare geopolymer concrete. strength tests, rapid freeze-thaw tests, and salt freeze resistance tests were carried out. Combined with pore structure analysis and the establishment of a damage model, key conclusions were drawn. In terms of mechanical properties, fly ash is beneficial for the subsequent strength development of concrete, while slag promotes early strength development. Polypropylene fibers can enhance the flexural and compressive strengths. Among them, the P60F20S20M1.2N12 mix ratio has the best performance, with a 28-day flexural strength of 6.5 MPa and a compressive strength of 45.3 MPa. In terms of freeze resistance, concrete’s resistance decreases as porosity and the proportion of harmful pores increase. The incorporation of fibers can inhibit deterioration of the pore structure, reduce the quality loss and relative dynamic elastic modulus caused by freeze-thaw, and increase the freeze resistance cycles of the four mix ratios by 25 times, 25 times, 25 times, and 50 times, respectively. The anti-salt freeze test shows that deicing salt aggravates freeze-thaw damage, while fibers can effectively resist the temperature stress and permeation pressure induced by salt freeze, thereby improving the anti-salt freeze effect. Based on the Lemaitre effect of strain variation, a freeze-damage equation for P60F20S20M1.2N12 fiber geopolymer concrete was established and can be used for freeze-damage evaluation. This research achievement provides an excellent fiber geopolymer concrete mix ratio scheme and theoretical support for pavement repair in seasonally frozen areas and new construction projects.

science.title: A Markov transition analysis to study changes in HIV prevention strategies among men who have sex with men in the French ANRS-PREVENIR cohort
science.description: Despite various biomedical and behavioral prevention strategies, new HIV seroconversions are disproportionately higher among gay and bisexual men who have sex with men (GBMSM). Using data from the French PrEP cohort ANRS-PREVENIR, this study aimed to investigate prevention strategies among this population and to analyze factors that may shape GBMSMs’ sexual behaviors. We defined three protection states as follows: self-dependent protection (SDP), which covered condom and/or PrEP use, partner-dependent protection (PDP), whereby the partner self-declared being either seronegative or seropositive with an undetectable viral load, and no protection (NP). We constructed a composite variable reflecting the degree of concordance between actual and perceived risk. A continuous-time multi-state Markov model was used to determine transition probabilities between protection states over time. Hazard ratios and their 95% confidence intervals (HR(95%CI)) were computed to identify factors associated with transitions. Irrespective of the protection state at baseline (i.e., SDP, PDP, NP), the highest Markov transition probabilities were to transition from one state to the same state at the next follow-up visit over the entire study period; specifically, the probability [95%CI] was 0.920 [0.916,0.924] for SDP, 0.783 [0.769,0.797] for PDP, and 0.584 [0.546,0.615] for NP. Event-driven PrEP (3.34(2.89–3.85)) and PrEP naivety (1.19(1.04–1.36)) were associated with an increased probability of transitioning from SDP to PDP. PrEP naivety (1.44(1.23–1.69)) and event-driven PrEP (4.15(3.47–4.96)) were also associated with an increased probability of transitioning from SDP to NP. A higher actual/perceived risk concordance score, i.e., higher actual risk and either a greater level of discordance or not considering risk, was associated with a reduced probability to transition from SDP to PDP (0.96 (0.92–0.99)), and was not associated with the transition from SDP to NP. Most GBMSM in our study transitioned from one state of protection to the same state at the next follow-up visit over the entire study period, highlighting the need for close counselling when GBMSM adopt a protection strategy for the first time, as it will shape their future strategies. Our findings also suggest that PrEP-naive and event-driven PrEP users have an increased probability of transitioning to protection strategies that are not self-controlled, raising questions about their vulnerability to HIV acquisition.

science.title: How You Squeeze Planetary Minerals Changes Everything
science.description: Studying the interiors of planets is essential for understanding planetary formation, evolution, and their ability to potentially host life as we know it. To accomplish this, researchers use a combination of Earth as an analog, computer models, meteorites, and data collected from other planetary bodies for studying their interior compositions. As a result, scientists have determined that the elements of magnesium and silicon are the most abundant planetary building blocks. And, under extreme pressures like the interior mantle of our planet, it forms magnesium oxide (MgO) crystals. But how does this same process occur under different pressures and temperatures on other planets like gas giants and larger rocky exoplanets called super-Earths?

science.title: GLTF-FEDformer: an adaptive time-frequency fusion method for multivariate time series anomaly detection enhanced by prediction error embedding
science.description: Multivariate time series are widespread in scenarios such as industrial IoT, smart manufacturing, energy systems, and medical monitoring. Their anomalous behaviors often involve complex patterns like long-range dependency changes, local dynamic shifts, transient spectral perturbations, and variable-association mismatches. Existing reconstruction-based and attention-based methods can learn the overall evolution of normal sequences but still lack fine-grained characterization of local time-frequency changes; moreover, relying solely on point-wise prediction errors for anomaly scoring struggles to fully reflect structural shifts in the error distribution. To address these issues, this paper proposes GLTF-FEDformer, a multivariate time series anomaly detection method that jointly models global and local time-frequency features. The method learns temporal dependencies, trend changes, and periodic candidate patterns from long-window contexts via a global temporal representation module, and enhances the modeling of temporal evolution through a continuous dynamic refinement mechanism. It also builds a lightweight local time-frequency feature extraction module that uses short-time Fourier transform, 2D convolutions, spectral gating, and inverse transforms to enhance the perception of local morphological changes, spectral perturbations, and time-frequency coupled features within local windows. A gated fusion mechanism performs data-dependent integration of global temporal information and local time-frequency information to obtain more discriminative prediction representations. Additionally, we design an anomaly scoring strategy based on a prediction-error-embedded profile, mapping prediction residuals into an embedding space and measuring structural deviations of test prediction-error embeddings from the normal error profile through variable-level standardized distances. The profile score is further combined with point-wise prediction errors to form anomaly responses with temporal localization ability. This strategy not only uses amplitude information of prediction errors but also captures structural shifts of the error distribution relative to normal patterns, thereby improving detection robustness in complex anomaly scenarios. Experimental results show the proposed method effectively enhances multivariate time series anomaly recognition and demonstrates strong detection performance and stability across various public datasets.
